parts.title: A winter in the Arctic
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last January, my aunt Mira flew to a small town in the north of Norway, where she works as a doctor for the winter. She sent us a long letter about her first week there.

The first thing she noticed was the darkness. For two months, the sun does not rise at all, and the town is lit only by street lamps and a blue light from the sky at midday. At first she felt sleepy all the time, but the local people gave her some advice: go out every day, eat fish and take a vitamin tablet.

She also had to learn to dress properly. "Wear three thin layers rather than one thick one," a neighbour told her. "Your own warmth stays between them." She laughed, but when she went out with just a coat, she was freezing within five minutes.

The best part, she writes, was the northern lights. One night, the sky turned green and then pink, and it moved like a ribbon. She stood in the snow for an hour and forgot the cold. She says she will come back next winter.

questions.explanation: The first thing she noticed was the darkness.

parts.title: Why is ice important?
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Ice covers about ten percent of the land on our planet. Most of it is found at the two poles, in the Arctic and in Antarctica. [1] Without it, the world would be a very different place.

First, ice helps to keep the Earth cool. Its white surface sends the sun's light back into space. [2] When the ice melts, the dark water absorbs more heat, and this makes the planet warmer.

Second, ice stores fresh water. About two thirds of all the fresh water on Earth is frozen in glaciers. [3] Millions of people depend on rivers that begin high in the mountains.

Third, ice is the home of many animals. Polar bears hunt seals on the sea ice. [4] If the ice disappears, they will lose their food and their place to live.

Scientists are watching the ice very carefully. [5] They use satellites to measure how fast it is changing every year.
sentences: This is a problem, because the bears cannot swim for ever.
It acts like a giant mirror at the top and bottom of the world.
They want to understand how it will change in the future.
The ice in the poles is more than three kilometres thick in some places.
This water slowly melts in the summer and flows down into the valleys.
Ice is very useful to human beings, although most of us never see it.

gaps.explanation: Ice is useful to human beings, and the next sentence says the world would be different without it.
It acts like a giant mirror, which explains the white surface and the light going back into space.
The water melts in summer and flows down; the next sentence mentions rivers.
The bears cannot swim for ever, so losing the ice is a problem.
They want to understand the change, and the next sentence says they use satellites.

parts.passage: Dear Gran, Greetings from Iceland! We arrived [1] Tuesday, and we are staying in a small wooden house near the sea. The weather is much colder [2] I expected, but the views are wonderful. Yesterday, we [3] a glacier, and I was amazed by its blue colour. The guide told us that the ice was thousands of years old. In the evening, we went to a hot spring, [4] was great after the cold day. I have taken hundreds of photographs, [5] I will show you when I come home. We are flying back on Sunday, and I [6] wait to tell you everything. Lots of love, Hannah

parts.title: Penguins
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. Instead, they use their wings [1] swim, and they are excellent swimmers. They spend most of their lives in the sea, and they only come onto the ice to rest or to have babies. The emperor penguin is the largest kind. It can grow to over one metre, [2] it is also the only penguin that breeds in the winter. The father keeps the egg warm on his feet for two months, while the mother goes to the sea to find food. During this time, he does not eat [3] all. When the chick is born, the mother comes back. Penguins live close together in big groups, [4] helps them to stay warm in the freezing wind. They take turns standing in the middle, [5] is the warmest place. In this way, nobody has to stay outside the whole time. Scientists say that penguins are an example of how animals can work [6] a team.

gaps.explanation: Use their wings to swim: purpose.
It can grow over one metre, and it is also the only one that breeds in winter.
Does not eat at all: a fixed phrase.
A big group, which helps them stay warm: a relative clause.
The middle, which is the warmest place.
Work as a team: a role.

parts.title: A talk about Antarctica
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: nathalie
turns.text: Good evening, everyone, and thank you for coming. I am Dr Eira Frost, and I spent eight months in Antarctica last year. It is the coldest, windiest and driest place on Earth. The lowest temperature ever recorded there was minus eighty-nine degrees. About thirty countries have research stations in Antarctica, but nobody lives there for ever. In the summer, about five thousand scientists work there, but in winter, the number is only one thousand. My job was to measure the thickness of the ice. Every week, I drove a snow vehicle for two hours to a special camp. Life is simple at the station. We ate together, and in the evenings we watched films or played cards. The thing I missed most was fresh fruit, because it takes a long time to reach the base. I would love to go back one day, and I recommend it to anyone who loves adventure.

gaps.explanation: I spent eight months in Antarctica.

gaps.explanation: The lowest temperature was minus eighty-nine degrees.

In winter the number is only one thousand.

gaps.prompt: Her job was to measure the thickness of the ___
gaps.explanation: My job was to measure the thickness of the ice.

parts.title: An interview with a polar guide
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Emrys, you take tourists to the Arctic. What do you enjoy most?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: The silence. When the engine stops, there is no sound except the wind and the ice moving. It is very peaceful.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Is your job dangerous?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: It can be. The weather changes quickly, and there are polar bears. That is why we always carry a radio and never go out alone.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you tell visitors before a trip?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: To dress in layers and to drink a lot of water. People forget to drink when it is cold, and that makes them tired.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Have you seen changes in the ice during your career?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Yes, many. Places where we used to walk are now open water. It makes me sad, but it also makes me want to teach people.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the funniest thing that has happened?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: A seal once climbed onto our boat and fell asleep in the front. We waited an hour for it to leave.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What are your plans for the future?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I am writing a book for children about life in the Arctic. I hope it will make young readers love the ice.
